title: Stalk going down for a finite normal map with dense etale source open
statement: Let X and Y be schemes, Y locally Noetherian, and f : X -> Y finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Assume every stalk of X and Y is a domain and integrally closed [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let V be an open of Y such that its inverse image is dense in X and the restriction of f over V is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Then for each x in X the local ring map O(Y,f(x)) -> O(X,x) has the going-down property: each prime below the contraction of a source prime lifts to a prime below that source prime.

source.place: Tags 00H8 (going down), 0357 (normal components), 01UA (openness of flat locally finitely presented maps); affine component argument in the proof of the supplied normalization boundary dimension transfer.

proof.text: Restrict to a normal integral affine component of the target around f(x). Finiteness makes its preimage affine and locally Noetherian. Normal components are open and closed, and there are finitely many in this quasi-compact preimage. Its section ring decomposes into their normal domain section rings as in normal_sections_finite_product (Tag 0357).

Density of the etale source open ensures that it meets every nonempty source component. The etale morphism on this open is flat and locally finitely presented, hence open (Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.UniversallyOpen, instance Flat.universallyOpen; Tag 01UA). Its component image is a nonempty open of the integral target component and is dense. Thus the finite map on each component is dominant; the corresponding map of domains is injective and integral.

Apply the normal-domain integral going-down instance (Tag 00H8) to each injective component algebra. Given primes in the localized target beneath the contraction of a localized source prime, contract them to the affine rings and apply going down inside the corresponding source prime. The resulting smaller prime is disjoint from the complement of the point prime and survives localization. Extension-contraction of prime ideals identifies its contraction with the prescribed localized target prime. Affine stalk localization isomorphisms transport this HasGoingDown property to f.stalkMap x. Empty source schemes have no points, so this case is vacuous.

lean.statement:
theorem finite_normal_dense_etale_stalk_goingDown {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsFinite f]
    (hY : ∀ y : Y, IsDomain (Y.presheaf.stalk y) ∧
      IsIntegrallyClosed (Y.presheaf.stalk y))
    (hX : ∀ x : X, IsDomain (X.presheaf.stalk x) ∧
      IsIntegrallyClosed (X.presheaf.stalk x))
    (V : Y.Opens) (hdense : Dense (↑(f ⁻¹ᵁ V) : Set X))
    (hetale : Etale (f ∣_ V)) (x : X) :
    letI := (f.stalkMap x).hom.toAlgebra
    Algebra.HasGoingDown (Y.presheaf.stalk (f x)) (X.presheaf.stalk x)
